newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee firmer, off highs after choppy trade.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee firmer, off highs after choppy trade.

text.p: London robusta coffee futures closed firmer but off earlier highs on Monday after a rollercoaster ride dominated by speculators and origin players.

A spurt of fund-inspired buying soon after the open drove benchmark July $135 higher to a fresh life-high of $2,190, sidelining origins who were content for the rally to reach its peak before taking profits.
London traders said they had expected July arabicas to open up to five cents/lb higher than Friday's close and continue last week's dizzy rally.
But although arabicas opened firmer, less than two cents up, origin players such as Colombia quickly moved in on the sell side and positions headed lower.
Sentiment on the London market, which had already edged back after the initial buying flurry, was dampened by New York and so origins sold positions, traders said.
"It's quite good for them at these levels," said one, adding that local selling had also been seen.
The lower levels then triggered another bout of speculator buying, driving July robustas back towards its earlier $2,190 peak -- and so the longs liquidated.
At the close July stood $45 higher at $2,100 after a wide trading range between $2,050 and $2,190.
All other positions ended sharply firmer, especially the further forwards such as January -- which was $128 up at $2,178. Overall volume was 6,010 lots.
Traders said they were monitoring news emerging from this week's London meeting of the Association of Coffee Producing Countries (ACPC) but awaited still harder news.
Delegates at the talks said a draft proposal for Wednesday's full session would have the group retain export quotas but include new flexibility on allocation.
The talks opened with a session of a technical group of Brazil, Colombia, Ivory Coast, Indonesia, Uganda and El Salvador which will put forward proposals for a full meeting on Wednesday.
